newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker on Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker on Greenspan comments.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker on Thursday, underperforming U.S. Treasuries, as fixed-income markets in both countries weakened following hawkish testimony by U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan, analysts said.
"Greenspan is talking the market in the direction he wants to go. He's doing a terrific job of it," said Philip Strathy, chief investment officer with Strathy Investments Inc.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.25 to C$108.60 to yield 7.260 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond, which managed to pare earlier losses following Greenspan's comments, closed up 8/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
The spread between the two widened to 30 basis points from 25 basis points at Wednesday's close.

Canadian and U.S. financial markets weakened after Greenspan told the Joint Economic Committee on Monetary Policy that inflation is likely to come under pressure from a tight labor market and stressed the Fed's need to act pre-emptively to keep inflation low.
Greenspan's comments weighed especially heavily on the Canadian dollar, as many analysts expect the Bank of Canada to keep Canadian rates unchanged if U.S. rates rise Tuesday.

Canada's currency weakened past the key C$1.38 (US$0.7246) support level following the comments. Canada's bond market underperformance relative to the U.S. market was "100 percent because of the dollar," said Strathy.
Canadian retail sales and merchandise trade surplus reports earlier this morning had little impact on Canadian bond prices, analysts said.

While Canadian bond investors will be paying close attention to the Canadian consumer price index data for February out tomorrow, analysts said the bond market will likely trade in a narrow range until Tuesday.
"It's unlikely that we're going to see anything happen ahead of Tuesday," said Jeoff Hall, Canadian analyst with Boston-based Technical Data. "We're just kind of on cruise control until the FOMC."
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.19 to C$102.58 to yield 6.633. The U.S. bond rose traded unchanged to yield 6.74 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 11 basis points from 13 basis points on Wednesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.17 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.34 percent.
